current_docstring_summary: Given one relation's KxK Z_scaled matrix, finds the column permutation maximizing matched (within-community) mass via Hungarian assignment on -|Z|. Returns permutation, is_identity, structure_score (min(matched)/max(unmatched); >1 means clean correctable mislabelling, <1 means genuine mixed coupling per FINDINGS §16), and diag_share_raw/diag_share_permuted (diagonal's share of total |Z| mass before/after permutation).
notable_facts: structure_score is float('inf') when max_unmatched <= 1e-15 (i.e. the off-diagonal, after masking out the matched cells, is essentially all zero) -- an edge case not mentioned in the docstring; callers comparing structure_score against a numeric threshold (e.g. relation_community_mass's threshold=1.0) will treat inf as always exceeding the threshold, i.e. always 'confidently correctable', which seems intended but is worth flagging as implicit behavior.

Module docstring (lines 58-62) attributes this function's centralization to 'previously copy-pasted across permutation_test.py and permutation_consistency_sweep.py' -- but per this audit's separate grep check, permutation_test.py in diagnostic_scripts/ still has its OWN local build_active_matrices/get_init (unrelated to this specific function) and was never confirmed here to actually import hungarian_diagonal_match either; this fact-file does not itself verify whether permutation_test.py currently imports hungarian_diagonal_match or still has its own copy of the matching logic -- flagging as a claim needing a targeted grep by whichever stage covers permutation_test.py specifically.

current_signature_or_value: def relation_share_matrix(mod, Z, U_f1, U_f2, structure_threshold, K):
current_docstring_summary: Generalizes production's own mod._relation_community_share (diagonal-only, length-K) to the full KxK permutation-corrected reconstruction-space share matrix for one relation, so off-diagonal (between-community) cells can be read on the same corrected basis as the diagonal. Uses production's own mod._hungarian_relabel_relation for the permutation/trust decision (same structure_score > structure_threshold gate) and the identical trace-based total-mass normalization. Self-checked elsewhere (z_scaled_offdiag_calibration_test.py) that this matrix's diagonal matches _relation_community_share exactly.
notable_facts: Docstring explicitly states a caveat rather than hiding it: total = trace(Z^T c_u Z c_v) is NOT in general equal to sum(Z_permuted**2) unless c_u/c_v are exactly identity (perfectly orthogonal unit-norm columns, not just unit-L2-norm) -- so THIS matrix's cells do not necessarily sum to exactly 1.0 the way the diagonal-only vector (_relation_community_share) is documented to. This is a genuine, self-disclosed limitation worth surfacing in any doc audit of what 'share' means for this function specifically vs. its diagonal-only sibling.

Depends on mod._hungarian_relabel_relation existing with the exact (perm, trusted) 2-tuple return contract this code assumes -- not independently re-verified in this extraction pass (out of scope, chunk13v9.py itself is covered by a different agent per the task's framing).

current_docstring_summary: Per-facet U_prob profile, unaggregated: for each active facet, the mean U_prob row (L1-normalized over K) across that facet's LIVE entities only, using mod.compute_probability_distributions(U_final). Exposed as the identical per-facet step membership_share_all_facets performs internally, BEFORE that function's own equal-weight pooling across all 9 facets -- so domain_balance_r_k can instead pool by domain. Facets with zero live entities are OMITTED from the returned dict, not nan-filled.
notable_facts: The 'omitted, not nan-filled' behavior for zero-live-entity facets is a real design choice with a downstream consequence: domain_balance_r_k (which consumes this function's output) will simply not see that facet in soc_facets/sem_facets at all, silently changing which facets contribute to a domain's weighted mean for that config -- there is no warning or flag surfaced when a facet drops out this way; a doc claim that 'all 9 facets contribute to domain balance in every config' would be inaccurate for any config/slice where a facet has zero live entities.

current_signature_or_value: def facet_relation_profile(config_id, Z_final, U_final, K, structure_threshold, exclude_anchors=False):
current_docstring_summary: The outer-loop/Z_scaled-reconstruction-space analog of facet_membership_profile. For each active facet, averages the per-relation share_r (production's mod._relation_community_share, permutation-corrected) over every relation touching that facet, then renormalizes to sum to 1. Each relation credits BOTH endpoint facets with its own share_r vector (documented as legitimate double-crediting, not double-counting, since it states a true fact about each). exclude_anchors=True gives a 'V2 sensitivity-floor variant' skipping anchor relations, to measure how anchor-carried a facet's profile is (V1 minus V2 = anchor sensitivity); V1 (anchors included, default) is stated as primary.
notable_facts: Fallback for a facet whose relation-share mean sums to ~0 is np.full(K, 1.0/K) (uniform) -- matching collapse_mass_share's uniform-fallback convention, NOT community_share_vector's raw-vector convention. Adds a third distinct fallback convention across this file's several share-computation functions (see F-DIAGBLOCKS-11/12's cross-reference) -- worth noting for anyone auditing consistency of near-zero-mass handling across the module.

exclude_anchors is a caller-supplied boolean with no default cross-check inside this function that V1 minus V2 is actually being computed correctly by any given caller -- the 'V1 primary, not V2' framing lives entirely in the docstring/plan reference, not enforced in code.

current_docstring_summary: Groups a dict[facet -> length-K profile] (from facet_membership_profile or facet_relation_profile) into social vs semantic sums via the module-level FACET_DOMAIN dict, then computes r_k = soc_k/(soc_k+sem_k+eps) and dev_k=|r_k-0.5| per community. weighting='equal' (every active facet in a domain contributes equally, described as matching collapse_mass_share/membership_share_all_facets's convention) or weighting='entity' (facet weighted by live entity count, requires live_counts). Returns a dict including which facets fed each domain, so an empty domain is visible rather than silently nan; returns all-None fields if either domain has zero contributing facets.
notable_facts: weighting='entity' requires live_counts to be passed and indexable by every facet name present in facet_profiles -- if live_counts is missing a facet that facet_profiles has, this raises a plain KeyError (np.array([live_counts[f] for f in facets])) with no more specific error message; a caller mismatch between the two dicts fails ungracefully.

CLAUDE.md's own §4.18 (E2/D2) records that the project settled on entity weighting as primary/decided, reversing an initial equal-weighting lean -- so while this function's docstring frames weighting='equal' as 'the codebase's established default,' the PROJECT-level decided default per CLAUDE.md is actually weighting='entity' for the domain-balance question specifically. This function's OWN default parameter value is weighting='equal', which is a real, checkable divergence between this function's default and the documented project decision -- exactly the kind of claim a later audit stage should verify against actual call sites (e.g. make_inloop_domain_balance_penalty_torch explicitly calls this pattern with entity weighting per its own docstring's 'D2' reference, but does NOT appear to call domain_balance_r_k directly at all -- it reimplements the weighted mean inline). Any doc claim of the form 'domain_balance_r_k defaults to the project's decided weighting' should be checked against this default='equal' fact.

This function is the one place in diagnostic_blocks.py that reads the module-level FACET_DOMAIN global (besides make_inloop_domain_balance_penalty_torch's own use of the differently-named/valued FACET_DOMAINS-vs-FACET_DOMAIN pair, see F-DIAGBLOCKS-08) -- confirms FACET_DOMAIN (social/semantic) is used by at least two functions, both domain-balance related.

current_signature_or_value: def verify_agreement(config_id="C6", K=4, lambda_l1=0.0, lambda_z_offdiag=0.05, slice_name="T1", write=True):
current_docstring_summary: Runs fit_production(init_mode='production') vs the real run_inner_solver reimplementation (fit_instrumented) on an identical config, reports agreement in epochs and math_loss, plus max absolute elementwise difference over U_final/Z_final/U_scales. Verdict is 'AGREE' if epochs match, math_loss absdiff < 1e-9, and both U_final/Z_final max absdiff < 1e-9; writes result to diagnostic_results/blocks_agreement_check.json when write=True. This is the module's own SESSION_PROTOCOL §E discharge mechanism, invoked via `python diagnostic_blocks.py --verify`.
notable_facts: The AGREE/DISAGREE verdict computation (line 1557-1558) checks epochs_match, math_loss_absdiff, max_absdiff_U_final, and max_absdiff_Z_final, but NOT max_absdiff_U_scales (computed at line 1546 and printed, but not included in the `ok` boolean) -- so a run where U_final/Z_final/math_loss/epochs all agree but U_scales diverges would still report VERDICT: AGREE. Given CLAUDE.md §4.3's finding that U_scales is an undetermined free gauge direction (small differences in U_scales are EXPECTED and not indicative of a real disagreement), excluding it from the verdict gate appears to be the deliberate, correct choice given that context -- but the module's own docstring/CLAUDE.md's ticket 79 finding is the only place that context lives; verify_agreement's own docstring here does not explain why U_scales is computed/printed but excluded from the pass/fail gate.

module docstring (lines 36-40) instructs 'Re-run after ANY edit to fit_instrumented or to run_inner_solver' -- this is a manual/human process requirement, not automatically enforced (no CI hook, pre-commit check, or version-bump gate visible anywhere in this file or in the BLOCKS_VERSION gating survey above) -- so the check being stale after an uncaught edit is a real possible failure mode with no automatic detection.

maxdiff() helper (lines 1527-1532) returns nan if sorted(a) != sorted(b) (mismatched key sets between production/instrumented output dicts) -- and nan compares as False in `< 1e-9`, so a KEY MISMATCH between the two fit paths' output dicts would silently produce VERDICT: DISAGREE (since nan < 1e-9 is False, ok becomes False) rather than a distinguishable 'key mismatch' error -- the printed reason would just say 'fit_instrumented has drifted' without indicating the specific failure mode was a missing/extra key rather than a numeric drift.
